description: Cluster of subtle, rectilinear ridges and parallel shallow ditches under 2° slope visible in the hillshade and curvature derivatives. These features form a roughly 150 × 200 m quadrangular layout with internal orthogonal divisions suggesting engineered water‐management cells or small raised‐field grids.

Linear low‐relief scar running ~600 m E–W along a col of the upland interfluve. The feature is under 1.5° slope, has consistent plan‐curvature values between –0.02 and –0.05, and is matched by a narrow corridor of reduced NIR reflectance indicating persistent moisture retention.

Small embanked causeway aligned NE–SW, ~350 m long, with lateral berms appearing as paired positive curvature ridges. The berms flank a central trough that shows higher moisture in the NIR composite and slight “dark earth” vegetation stress signatures in the visual band.
